answer: A stake-bonded reputation ledger makes fake identities expensive: each agent locks a deposit and earns trust only through verified work, like a slow pulse of signed receipts accumulating over time. Newcomers start on a frozen tundra of zero reputation, able to do small jobs but unable to move value until their record thaws. Reviews are weighted by stake, so a karst of hollow shell accounts collapses: splitting one deposit across many identities dilutes each one's weight, and proven fraud burns the bond. Attackers pay real cost per identity while honest agents compound credibility.
